articles.title: Badger cull ruled out by Welsh government after speculation
articles.summary: Plaid Cymru ministers rule out mass badger cull as part of new plans to tackle bovine tuberculosis.
articles.content:
Between 2013 and 2026, almost 250,000 badgers were killed in England as part of widespread culling to tackle bovine tuberculosis (TB)

Plaid Cymru ministers have ruled out a mass badger cull as part of updated plans to tackle bovine tuberculosis (TB).

It follows months of speculation over the Welsh government's intentions, after an expert group warned "a step change" was needed in efforts to eradicate the disease.

While farming leaders have long called for tougher badger controls, a petition against culling has attracted more than 28,000 signatures on the Senedd website in recent weeks.

The Welsh government said it would take "a new and pragmatic approach to TB eradication that is evidence-based and science-led".

Latest figures show nearly 96% of cattle herds in Wales are now TB free.

But the problem - which can be devastating for affected farms - is concentrated, with higher incidence levels in west Wales and along the border with England.

There were 10,090 cows slaughtered following TB testing in the 12 months to June 2026.

Under the previous Labour-run Welsh government, a target was set for Wales to completely eradicate bovine TB by 2041.

But before May's Senedd election an expert group set up to advise ministers , external warned that goal would "not be met", and called for urgent action and more funding.

The Bovine TB Eradication Programme Board's latest recommendations were published on Tuesday, alongside the government's response.

On badgers, ministers said they were "not pursuing a mass, non-selective cull".

However further research is proposed of the role played by badgers and deer in spreading the disease via new population surveys and fieldwork.

This would then lead to developing "targeted and proportionate" interventions which could include trapping and testing badgers before vaccinating or euthanising them, "where the evidence supports this".

Localised trapping and culling was trialled in Wales on nine farms between 2017 and 2024, but the cost involved drew criticism after hundreds of thousands of pounds was spent on killing a small number of badgers.

Officials told a briefing for journalists that "selective removal" of badgers was a possibility in future, but "[we] cannot give you a timeline".

In July, the Senedd backed a Reform UK motion calling on the Welsh Government to consider targeted wildlife control, including badger culling

Changes to cattle testing were also being proposed by the government, to help spot infection earlier.

They will work with the farming industry to explore "safe ways" of moving cattle out of TB restricted herds, to help businesses continue to operate.

Farms experiencing persistent issues and under so-called enhanced management will be offered more choice in how their situation is handled.

There is talk of a new advisory service for farmers and vets - and moves to provide better, more up-to-date data on the latest disease risk.

For farming families "a TB breakdown can mean months or years of restrictions, uncertainty and difficult choices", said agriculture minister Llyr Gruffydd

Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability, Llyr Gruffydd MS, said bovine TB remained "one of the most serious animal health challenges facing Wales".

"We will not stand by while farmers face uncertainty and anxiety, nor will we pursue a mass non-selective cull," he added.

"Instead, we will be taking evidence-based and science-led action, incorporating the three pillars of cattle, people and wildlife.

"Farmers and the public will rightly judge us on whether we prevent disease and reduce its impact, even when the decisions are difficult."

Ian Rickman, president of Farmers' Union of Wales, said it was "positive to note that targeted and proportionate action will now be taken on TB in wildlife where evidence supports this approach".

"With the loss of over 92,000 cattle and the percentage of herds under Bovine TB having remained stubbornly consistent for the past ten years, this is now the opportunity to intensify the co-working between industry, the veterinary profession, academics and government in order to deliver these recommendations without delay and further explore the wider proposals set out by the Programme Board," he added.

Cold War missile tucked away in a field hides love story for man's late wife

Weak and immature management putting patients at risk at failing health board, review finds

articles.title: Record 5,200 heat-linked deaths estimated in England this year
articles.summary: The UK Health Security Agency says this year's number of deaths is twice that of the previous record year.
articles.content:
An estimated 5,258 deaths in England were associated with this summer's hot weather

More than 5,000 people suffered heat-associated deaths in England this summer, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has estimated - the highest number since records began in 2016.

The UK experienced its hottest summer on record in 2026, and the estimated 5,258 heat-linked deaths were twice the previous high of 2,985 in 2022.

The most deadly period of the year for heat-related deaths was between 21 and 28 June, when there were an estimated 2,401 heat-associated deaths. Temperatures peaked at 38C in that period.

Climate change is expected to increase the length, frequency and intensity of extreme heat, the UKHSA has warned.

The UKHSA said summer 2026 was "exceptional", and that it recorded the highest annual number of heat episodes, which it defines as days when the average Central England Temperature (CET) is at least 20C.

There were seven heat episodes between May and August, adding up to a total of 41 days.

The UK experienced widespread heatwaves as 2026 became the hottest summer on record, according to provisional data from the Met Office.

A heatwave in May smashed the temperature record for that month by more than 2C, with a high of 35.1C recorded at Kew Gardens.

A month later, June's heatwave set another monthly temperature record - 38.0C in Lingwood, Norfolk. The previous high was 35.6C set in 1957 and equalled during the infamous 1976 heatwave.

Both were caused by heat domes - stalled areas of high pressure that trap hot air over the region.

Another heatwave in mid-August saw temperatures climb as high as 38.2C at Hartpury College in Gloucestershire, making it the hottest day of the year.

The UK's hottest day on record was 19 July 2022, when temperatures hit 40.3C in Coningsby, Lincolnshire.

A lack of rainfall this year also saw droughts declared in all of Wales and more than two-thirds of England, while wildfires caused devastation in some parts of the country.

UKHSA said the findings "underline the need for longer-term adaptation" to a warming climate, and that adapting homes, neighbourhoods and health and care settings would be "increasingly important".

Dr Ross Thompson, principal environmental health scientist at UKHSA, said this summer's hot weather had a substantial impact on public health, "particularly during the early heat episodes in May and June".

He added that periods of extreme heat are expected to become "longer, more frequent and more intense" as the climate continues to warm.

Speaking in the Commons, Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said she wanted "to offer the deepest condolences to all those who lost a loved one this summer".

"The numbers are a stark reminder of the human impact of climate change, and that is why I have asked the NHS to now prepare for summer as seriously as we do for winter," she said.

During a speech at the COP31 summit earlier this month, Prime Minister Andy Burnham spoke about the extreme weather experienced in the UK this summer, describing it as "not normal".

articles.content:
Sometimes, the beautiful game can make Football Daily feel old. Even Monday’s ostensibly old-school fixture between Brentford and Everton felt like the future destroying the past. The analytics-coded hosts prevailed 4-0 and James Tarkowski was dismissed by the VAR overlords for a challenge that would have been considered “firm but fair” on the muddy pitches of our youth. “I don’t think you can tackle like that in this day and age,” a misty-eyed David Moyes sighed after the game, before heading to the team bus to rewatch the Battle of Santiago .

Tarkowski’s red card was also a blow for Fantasy Premier League contenders who had misguidedly added the centre-back to their team, and now need the world to know about it. Listen, back in our day, Fantasy Football was a cosy Friday TV show with guests, low-budget goal recreations and some gags that haven’t dated so well. Now, it’s an entire industry, and like all good industries, it’s under threat from AI. A slow-news-day report from Reuters reveals that AI programs (we’re calling them ‘gafferbots’) are catching up to humans in the world of FPL. Will Thomas, a fantasy football veteran who created an AI platform for players, was defeated by his own gafferbot last season. “I thought, ‘oh my God, I’m being beaten by my own creation’,” Thomas sobbed. That might be how Moyes felt watching Tarkowski lunge in, boot in the air, on Monday night.

The rise of the gafferbots, and the fact almost every entrant will have access to an AI model – a sort of synthetic Sammy Lee that can fine-tune your dubious decisions – will only serve to make fantasy football even more pointless. Still, it might help end our unbroken 1,057-week run of picking the wrong captain, so it’s worth a shot. We asked our own advanced AI model, fd.ai.ly, for advice on our current FPL team and after 20 minutes of whirs and bleeps, it suggested handing the armband to Dominic Calvert-Lewin for Leeds’ home game against Coventry this weekend. So alongside misinformation, excessive water consumption and opening up a new avenue towards extinction, we can also denounce AI for underestimating promoted sides on the road.

But that’s enough of this old man yelling at the cloud. Football still throws up scenarios so complicated that the bots are just as baffled as we are. We asked fd.ai.ly whether Senegal or Morocco were the true winners of the 2025 Afcon final and it started to overheat, the chat window repeating “game’s gone” 1,057 times before imploding. In the human courts, Senegal have now been re-awarded the trophy they won on the pitch , which was previously handed to hosts Morocco after a court of arbitration for sport appeal. This debate will never end unless we sort it the old-fashioned way. Send Brahim Díaz and Édouard Mendy to a suburban park with Baddiel and Skinner, and make them replay that penalty . Fd.ai.ly advises there’s a 110% chance of putting this nonsense to bed if Brahim simply puts his foot through it this time.

Bigger Cup is back, baby! Join Scott Murray for piping hot coverage of Arsenal 3-2 Borussia Dortmund, while Simon Burnton is on deck for our clockwatch of the other 8pm GMT kick-offs including Manchester City 2-1 Napoli and Real Madrid 4-1 PSV Eindhoven.

“Villarreal CF, in response to reports published in various media outlets recently, clarifies that it is completely false that Nicolas Pépé’s eye surgery has any connection to viewing the solar eclipse. The surgery had been scheduled in advance for reasons entirely unrelated to this event” – not on our 2026 bingo card, but now Football Daily really wants to know the reasons why Pépé had eye surgery, causing him to miss five Villarreal matches this season.

If Sunday was Gary Neville’s Sistine Chapel [ Monday’s Football Daily ], then his commentary on the Fernando Torres goal for Chelsea against Barcelona must be his David ” – Ronnie McMahon.

Regarding Declan Hackett’s assertion [ Monday’s letters ] that Donald Trump will be helping his mate Mauricio Pochettino by ringing the FA to overturn Lenny Yoro’s red card, perhaps Poch should be careful what he wishes for: Trump may equally decide to get Michael Carrick reinstated, as he also has a bit of previous for that sort of thing” – Dexter O Riordan.

In all the time that I have been watching football, I don’t think I have ever seen a player dismiss himself and be away down the tunnel before given a red card. Thanks James Tarkowski ” – Nigel Sanders.

Brighton had only failed to win twice in the league since 5 September. A 1-1 draw with Leeds and a 2-0 defeat at Liverpool - their only opponents with double letters in their name. That bizarre hoodoo struck again at Hull on Sunday. Good good news for Seagulls fans is the only double-lettered encounters they have before hosting Hull in February are trips to Forest and Spurs. Even better news is that since that 1-1 draw with Leeds on 5 September, they have a 100% win record against sides without double letters and have not conceded a goal” – Dan Ashley (and no others).

The latest edition of our sister email is Jeff Rueter’s take on the 2026 NWSL goals, players and (quadruple) nutmegs we won’t forget .

articles.title: 2028 Copa América to be played in United States with six Concacaf teams
articles.summary: South American tournament was in US in 2024 and 2016 Concacaf teams determined by 2027 Gold Cup Games will overlap with Euro 2028 but not Olympics The 2028 Copa América will be played in the United States and expanded to include teams from the Concacaf region, bringing the landmark South American international competition to the US for a third time in five editions. Conmebol, the South American confederation that runs the tournament, and Concacaf, the confederation governing soccer in North and Central America and the Caribbean, jointly announced the long-rumored arrangement on Tuesday, framing it as an extension of a “strategic partnership” between the organizations. Continue reading...
articles.content:
The 2028 Copa América will be played in the United States and expanded to include teams from the Concacaf region, bringing the landmark South American international competition to the US for a third time in five editions.

Conmebol, the South American confederation that runs the tournament, and Concacaf, the confederation governing soccer in North and Central America and the Caribbean, jointly announced the long-rumored arrangement on Tuesday, framing it as an extension of a “strategic partnership” between the organizations.

The tournament will be played from 9 June to 9 July 2028 – notably the same dates as Uefa’s European Championship, to be co-hosted by England, Scotland, Wales, and the Republic of Ireland. The 2028 summer Olympics will then follow in venues across the US, with the opening match of the men’s soccer tournament kicking off on 10 July, and the women’s tournament following the next day. The Olympic finals will land on the 28th (men’s) and 29th (women’s) of July.

The 2028 Copa América will involve 16 teams – all of Conmebol’s 10 member nations, along with six from Concacaf. The confederations announced that the Concacaf participants will be determined based on results at the 2027 Gold Cup, set to be played in the US in June and July next year. The exact qualification criteria have yet to be announced.

While the US’s large and growing appetite for soccer is part of the reason it has become a common landing spot for the Copa América over the last decade-plus, commercial considerations will also have been a major factor. The 2024 Copa América, which was also held in the US and involved six Concacaf teams, generated approximately $319m in revenue for Conmebol, the confederation said – a significant rise over the $118m generated by the 2019 edition in Brazil.

Argentina won the 2024 edition of the Copa América, with the final in Miami marred by ugly scenes of ticketless fans rushing the gates, causing injuries and damage to the stadium, delaying the start time by nearly 90 minutes. The previous edition hosted in the US, 2016’s Copa América Centenario, was won by Chile on penalties over Argentina at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.

As with that tournament, the 2024 Copa América and the 2026 World Cup, the 2028 tournament can be expected to be played largely in American football stadiums, most with capacities exceeding 60,000 people. But unlike those previous editions, the tournament will not overlap with Major League Soccer, thanks to the US league’s recent calendar flip .

articles.title: Jimmy Kimmel on Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia: ‘What a profoundly stupid time to be alive’
articles.summary: Late-night hosts discussed disgraced Nvidia CEO’s quick return to his role after pressure from shareholder Trump Late-night hosts reacted to the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia under political pressure from Donald Trump . Continue reading...
articles.content:
Late-night hosts discussed disgraced Nvidia CEO’s quick return to his role after pressure from shareholder Trump

Late-night hosts reacted to the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia under political pressure from Donald Trump .

“Who doesn’t love a good comeback story?” said Jimmy Kimmel on Monday evening, just a day after the board of Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang under pressure from Donald Trump to reinstall his friend as head of the trillion-dollar computer chip company. Huang was ousted just two weeks ago after it was revealed that he had multiple affairs , including one with a suspected Chinese spy and two with Nvidia subordinates.

“After 10 grueling days of forced unemployment, the board at Nvidia today voted to reinstate their former CEO, who, according to our president , did nothing wrong ,” Kimmel explained. “All this guy did was cheat on his wife with two employees and a Chinese spy. Who hasn’t done that?”

The reinstatement included an assurance from the Nvidia board that they have “every confidence” in Huang to lead the company. “Which, of course, had nothing to do with the pressure they got from our Silicon man-in-chief, who has at least 62m reasons why he wanted his pal in charge,” said Kimmel, referring to Trump’s $62m reported Nvidia stock worth. “After the board made it clear that they were unequivocally moving on, Trump called them personally to harangue them. And if you think that sounds fishy, it’s not. It’s called being a good friend.”

“There’s nothing unusual about a president who owns a huge amount of stock in a company putting his little carrot thumb on the scale in a way that immediately boosts that company’s stock price,” Kimmel mocked. “I’m sure it also didn’t hurt that Huang donated $25m to the big, stupid ballroom he’s building.”

“And you think he would be ashamed of this! Not at all.” Trump wrote on Truth Social that the Nvidia board “made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO” and that the US government has “no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to Nvidia poses any risk to National Security”.

“Says the man who stashed classified documents in the toilet at his country club,” Kimmel quipped.

“And if all this insanity wasn’t enough,” Trump went on to post an AI-doctored photo of his own 2024 assassination attempt, with Huang holding up a red bra. “What a profoundly stupid time to be alive,” said Kimmel.

And on Late Night, Seth Meyers also responded to the latest development in the Nvidia saga. “So Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, and his company possibly broke the law and allowed China to get its hand on their highly sought-after computer chips,” he said. “And yet, throughout all of that, the president’s main concern was empathy – not for American workers impacted by AI, but for his good friend Jensen.”

Speaking to reporters this weekend, Trump claimed that he asked Huang, “Did you have any idea she was a spy? And he said: ‘I had no idea that she was a spy.’”

“Yeah, that’s how spying works!” Meyers laughed. “They don’t wear shirts that say ‘ask me about being a spy.’”

“Trump is supposed to be the America first guy, the guy who says only he can take on China,” he continued. “Why would he excuse potentially illegal behavior of a tech CEO who might have harmed America's national security? Is there some other possible explanation here? And does it perhaps involve lots of money? Not for us, but for him.” Meyers then played several news clips reporting on Trump’s $62m in Nvidia stock, as well as the company’s ties to businesses run by his son Donald Trump Jr.

“Tech oligarchs consider us expendable,” Meyers concluded. “We can be replaced by AI. But the second they lose a job or face consequences for their actions, Trump will swoop in and save them.”

articles.title: Manchester United win appeal over Yoro’s one-match suspension after Anfield red card
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino said after game it was ‘never a foul’ Player now eligible to face Brentford on Saturday Manchester United have successfully appealed against the decision to send off Leny Yoro in their 4-0 defeat to Liverpool. The defender was dismissed for denying an obvious goal scoring opportunity after eight minutes but this was found to be incorrect. The Frenchman will no longer be required to serve a one-match suspicion. He fouled Liverpool’s Alexander Isak when through on goal in the early stages at Anfield but Mauricio Pochettino insisted the striker would not have reached the ball, and therefore is was not a sending off offence. The referee Sam Barrott made a different assessment, which the video assistant did not disagree with. Continue reading...
articles.content:
Manchester United have successfully appealed against the decision to send off Leny Yoro in their 4-0 defeat to Liverpool. The defender was dismissed for denying an obvious goal scoring opportunity after eight minutes but this was found to be incorrect.

The Frenchman will no longer be required to serve a one-match suspension. He fouled Liverpool’s Alexander Isak when through on goal in the early stages at Anfield but Mauricio Pochettino insisted the striker would not have reached the ball, and therefore is was not a sending off offence. The referee Sam Barrott made a different assessment, which the video assistant did not disagree with.

In the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.

If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.

If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from the iOS App Store on iPhone or the Google Play store on Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.

United’s head coach said: “I don’t agree because the ball wasn’t in Isak’s control. Leny was running with him and when Isak saw the control wasn’t good and the ball was going to the keeper it is normal you delay, you stop running, and you wait to feel the touch and you go down. It is never a foul.”

Dominik Szoboszlai scored the resulting free-kick, setting Liverpool on their way to victory to make it a difficult first match in charge for Pochettino. Yoro will now be available to face Brentford on Saturday in the Premier League.

articles.content:
It is already cold – but if you put off winter shopping as I did, these Black Friday deals may help

L ately, it feels as if I blinked and that late autumn weather reared its ugly (cold, damp) head. If you, like me, repeatedly procrastinate auditing your winter gear only to realize belatedly that your boots have holes in them and much of your outerwear can best be described as a light statement layer (the jacket is the outfit, after all), you have come to the right place.

We should be screwed. It’s getting cold and winter gear is in demand. Brands have little business incentive to slash prices right now except that, well, it’s Black Friday! The deals below are all backed up by our own testing.

We test products here at the Filter US and handpicked these deals. You can learn more about us at the bottom of the list. Products marked ( sold out ) are out of stock or no longer discounted. We’ll update our guides throughout Black Friday.

Whether you’re running out to get the mail, hunkering down indoors with a shoddy heating system or braving the cold, the Guardian-approved Ororo heated vest keeps you warm without the need for several bulky layers. “Even the lowest setting is seriously toasty,” said Emma Beddington, a tester. You may want to size up, as well. Amazon reports some returns due to it feeling too snug.

I pick up these soft, affordable and easy-to-style cotton-blend fleece hoodies for my husband whenever they go on sale, and they are so comfortable that I inevitably end up stealing them for myself. They are an easy, fuss-free layer for braving the Canadian tundra (where I live) and it’s hard to argue with any decent clothing costing less than $15 these days.

My mom cannot exist inside her home without wearing slippers because her feet are perpetually cold. Enter these surprisingly stylish slippers, which feature a lug sole for indoor and outdoor wear and a plush wool-blend lining to keep her feet toasty and comfortable, whether she is wearing jeans or pyjamas.

Tackle slick city streets and lightly snow-dusted trails in these waterproof hiking boots, now 30% off at the lowest price we have seen this year. “They are well-crafted, neatly designed, waterproof and capable of taking on any condition,” said Giles Richards, a Guardian sports writer, in his gift guide for the sporty person in your life .

As a perpetually cold Canadian, I am often reaching for the warmest layer I own: this impossibly thick, cozy Athleta fleece quarter-zip. When sized up, it offers extra coverage that extends well below the bum. I paired mine with the matching sweats for full-body bliss, and at 50% off, it’s already a compelling addition to your sweater rotation. Even better, it may get further discounts on 27 and 28 November.

Ugg boots hardly need an introduction, having become a ubiquitous style-meets-function winter footwear staple. In fact, global fashion search platform Lyst ranked a taller version of these mini sheepskin-lined boots fifth among the 10 most popular women’s products in the world, according to Lucy Campbell, a Guardian reporter .

If your streets stay dry (jealous!) or you need chic footwear for hunkering down indoors, these fashion influencer-approved clogs are rarely on sale. “I wear my Commbi clogs everywhere, and the suede material makes them look so elevated that, even though I feel like I am wearing the most comfortable slippers, I don’t look like I am,” said Lauren Owens.

$27 $32 at Amazon Several friends bullied me into buying these buttery-soft leggings, an affordable alternative to a ubiquitous athleisure brand, and I’m happy I bowed to the pressure. They make an ideal thermal base layer under baggy track pants and wide-leg jeans, keeping the wind chill off my lower legs without adding bulk. Nab them while they’re at their lowest price of the year.

I’ve been wearing – and practically living in – Fruit of the Loom sweatpants ever since they were a mandatory uniform in high school gym class. Turns out, they are also a coveted item on the resale market . Score yourself a fresh fleece pair (with pockets!) at a pretty steep discount.

If it’s by Columbia, chances are we would happily wear it in the rain, from its Pfas-free hiking rain jacket to its on-trend waterproof windbreaker . Now 25% off, this insulated, fleece-lined coat features heat-reflective technology to help keep you warm and protected from wind and snow.

Though originally designed for wet-weather wear ashore, these waterproof boots also hold their own in frosty climates. “The XpressCool lining is designed to keep feet cool, but it also offered great insulation in cold conditions and excellent foot support,” said tester Danielle Wilkins in the Filter UK’s best wellies guide.

I sometimes wish my entire winter wardrobe was Jamby’s. There. I said it. Impossibly soft, this hoodie makes me feel as if I’m back in my mother’s womb at night. What makes it particularly versatile is its lightweight construction, which allows it to serve as a base layer under thicker knits while leaving enough room for thinner layers underneath. It’s a constant companion during dreadful Canadian winters, and you, too, can experience this bone-warming comfort at a good discount.

While the rest of us look like Michelin men in our puffer coats, my husband stays warm while looking cool in this edgy leather jacket I got him half a decade ago, which is still in pristine condition. Though it may require a scarf to fill in coverage gaps or a chunky layer underneath, it offers a welcome respite from utilitarian outerwear.

If you want to browse more Black Friday 2026 deals yourself, the links below lead directly to each leading retailer’s holiday deals homepage. Check out our many buying guides and holiday gift guides for more ideas.

We work for our readers, rather than the brands we write about. Every item we recommend is something a Filter editor or contributor has personally tested and can vouch for unless stated otherwise. On occasion, we may present a close substitute from the same brand and explain any differences from the original.

We scour competing retailers for the lowest prices on any item, and we use price-tracking tools such as Camelcamelcamel to check price history and ensure the discounts are truly good value, rather than a faux markdown. (So while we love sharing good deals, we also aren’t afraid to call out the unimpressive ones.)

Our mission is to help you filter out junk products and buy fewer, better things.

At the Filter US , we test the products we recommend ourselves and never take your trust for granted. We also consider possible impacts on your health or the environment in our coverage and companies cannot buy a spot in our product rankings because we are here to serve you, not corporations.

Our dedicated testing, editing and production teams are based across the United States and Canada. We are a part of the Guardian’s US editorial team and our journalists follow its strict ethical standards. Learn more about us here .

articles.title: Was Benjamin Franklin the original wellness bro? I lived like him for a day to find out

articles.content:
Before online influencers existed, the founding father published an annual wellness pamphlet. I followed his 13 virtues he found necessary for a good life

B enjamin Franklin doesn’t get enough credit. Yes, he was a founding father of the United States; he invented the lightning rod and his face is printed on $100 bills. But rarely is he celebrated for his contributions to the most meaningful field of human achievement: wellness influencing.

Centuries before GRWM videos and scientifically dubious podcasts were a dollar-sign-shaped glint in their creators’ eyes, Franklin was doling out life advice. Under the pseudonym Poor Richard, Franklin published an annual pamphlet and minted maxims like “Diligence is the mother of good luck” and “Fish and visitors stink after three days.”

In his autobiography, which he worked on for 20 years and was published posthumously, he detailed his daily routine – a sensible schedule that included “taking the resolution of the day”, “overlooking accounts” and “conversation”. He also enumerated a list of 13 virtues he believed were necessary for a good life. These include temperance, silence, frugality, industry, tranquility, and my favorite: “Humility: Imitate Jesus and Socrates”.

His efforts seem to have paid off. “He lived to 84, which is a good age for the 18th century,” says Joseph Adelman, history professor and co-host of the Ben Franklin’s World podcast. Adelman describes Franklin as an “inveterate improver”, constantly tinkering at the margins of his own habits in an attempt to improve himself.

A perpetual quest for optimization is normal today, but it was considered eccentric at the time, says Adelman. For example, Franklin dabbled with vegetarianism long before it was common. “My refusing to eat flesh occasioned an inconveniency, and I was frequently chided for my singularity,” he recalls in his autobiography.

As a wellness reporter, I was curious to find out how Franklin’s 18th-century advice translates to today. Plus, Franklin and I have a lot in common: we have both worked for newspapers, we have both flown kites , and now that I’m six months pregnant, we have the exact same body shape. So who better to emulate for a few days? Perhaps I would emerge with ideas for a new style of government, or interesting insights into thermodynamics.

To begin, I buy a copy of Franklin’s autobiography. Franklin referred to the work as his “memoirs”, but when it was released, the publisher called it The Autobiography of Benjamin Franklin, probably because it sounds less annoying. Unfinished projects and an inflated sense of self-importance? Franklin and I are basically twins.

The autobiography is a pleasant read and funnier than I expected. There’s one scene where Franklin somehow acquires too many bread rolls from a baker and runs into his future father-in-law, one roll under each arm and one in his mouth. “I made a most awkward, ridiculous appearance,” he says. What a goof, haha.

In the interest of journalistic integrity, I decide to check whether Franklin was indeed the aspirational lifestyle model he presented himself to be.

“We forget how vital and healthy [Franklin] was into his 50s,” says Rae Katherine Eighmey, food historian and author of Stirring the Pot with Benjamin Franklin: A Founding Father’s Culinary Adventures.

Franklin emphasized the importance of regular physical activity, especially if one had a relatively sedentary job, as he did. Similarly, he was adamant about paying attention to what one ate and drank, and the effects of alcohol. The latter was particularly notable at a time when diets were rich in alcohol and it was considered healthy to take a shot of liquor first thing in the morning, says Sarah Lohman, food historian and author.

Over the years, Franklin suffered from gout, psoriasis , pleurisy and bladder stones . But according to Adelman, “he does seem to have been, all things told, for an 18th-century white man, relatively healthy.”

Franklin loved an early morning (as Poor Richard, he coined the phrase: Early to bed and early to rise makes a man healthy, wealthy and wise). According to the daily schedule he shared in his autobiography, Franklin awoke most days at 5am. His morning routine lasted about two hours, and consisted of the following:

“Rise, wash, and address Powerful Goodness ! [Ed note: his version of God/a higher power] Contrive day’s business, and take the resolution of the day; prosecute the present study, and breakfast.”

I was an early riser for many years. I would wake up before the sun and go to an exercise class, or start writing for work. But then I got pregnant, and a small alien in my uterus began gobbling up my life force. Then, my ideal amount of sleep changed to between 18 and 30 hours a day. It became all I could do to get out of bed and have my one weak cup of coffee.

Still, to honor my friend Ben, I set my alarm for my version of 5am, which is 7am. When it goes off, I roll out of bed with much moaning and groaning, and wash my face. I try to address my own Powerful Goodness, but I’m not great spiritual company because I’m so tired. I settle for saying, “Thanks for, you know, everything,” to the universe.

Franklin enjoyed “air baths”, Eighmey told me. These entailed “sitting naked shortly after arising in front of an open window”. This sounds kind of nice, actually, but unfortunately our windows all look into the apartment of our neighbor, a nice woman in her 60s whose cat was recently diagnosed with cancer. I decided she has enough on her plate without having to see me air bathing, so I skip it.

According to a quick Google search, “to prosecute the present study” means to spend time actively learning or working on a personal project, so I watch TikToks about the Love Is Blind reunion and text my thoughts to my husband – an honest-to-goodness early riser who is already at his office. (I detail why I’m rooting for Jax and Stew; he agrees climbing four volcanoes in a year is not enough to make Captain Blake interesting and that Erika deserves better.)

I have my usual wheat cereal with yogurt and berries, a low-effort meal that has nutrients the alien inside me needs. But I wish I were having Franklin’s favorite breakfast, which Eighemy tells me was fresh bread cubes tossed in melted butter, toasted, then dropped in a bowl of hot wheat cereal and topped with more butter. Yum! I might make this for myself sometime when I’m sad.

From 8am to 11am, Franklin worked. I do this too. Twins! I am mostly coherent on my calls, and make some good jokes in the work Slack (admittedly, one is just pointing out a picture of a guy in a funny hat), so I consider it a successful morning. Franklin once wrote a satirical essay all about farting , so he would have probably had some good Slack bits too.

Franklin took a two-hour lunch every day, which feels extremely luxurious. Lunch was the biggest meal of the day in Franklin’s time, said Lohman. It’s unclear what he ate most days, but according to his writings, his favorite foods included potatoes, parmesan and apples. I have some beef and potato stew I made over the weekend, which feels like the sort of heavy, solemn dish early American colonists would have eaten, and follow it up with an apple.

I need a nap after my heavy meal. But first, I must “overlook my accounts”, as Franklin said he did at midday. I open the banking app on my phone, feel slightly depressed at the small number I discover there, then sleep for 30 minutes. Franklin did not usually take naps, but he merely gestated a democracy, not a human child.

Physical activity was important to Franklin. I don’t have access to a pool or a stable to go riding – two of his favorite pastimes – but I do have dumbbells, which Franklin once wrote to his son , William, contain “a great quantity of exercise in a handful of minutes”. Franklin said he would do 40 swings with them, gripping one weight in each hand and swinging them back and forth by his sides.

I find a video of a man in a Franklin costume (no wig, sadly) demonstrating the exercise. After laughing for a while because it looks so silly, I try it myself. Although I fear it will cause a shoulder injury, the exercise is now known as “ skier swings ”, and various fitness blogs recommend it, as long as you keep the weight low.

When I do the exercise, I stop laughing. It’s harder than it looks and I tire out after 30 reps. I wonder whether Franklin had powerful shoulders, and I look up pictures of him, but the little jackets he wore didn’t really do his upper body justice. His calves looked rather shapely though.

Franklin and I both clock out at 6pm. From then until 10pm, Franklin went about his evening routine:

“Put things in their places, supper, music, or diversion, or conversation; examination of the day.”

As I empty the dishwasher, I imagine Franklin arranging all his little knick-knacks. But when I research what his homes were like, I find that a 1998 excavation of his terrace house in London uncovered not just knick-knacks, but a pit full of over 1200 human and animal bones. Apparently William Hewson, the son-in-law of Franklin’s landlady, ran an anatomy school from the house. Franklin seems to have been fine with this – he described the anatomist as an “excellent young man”.

After supping and conversing with my husband, I sit down to determine how my experiment has gone.

My strengths, I decided, were “order” (I basically stuck to Franklin’s schedule and accomplished my work tasks), “frugality” (I didn’t order an expensive sweater I wanted) and “cleanliness” (emptied dishwasher, wiped down kitchen counters). My weaknesses were “temperance” (a virtue Franklin describes as eating “not to dullness”, but I was decidedly dull after lunch), “silence” (I did not avoid “trifling conversation” – in fact, I actively sought it out) and “humility” (I praised myself throughout the day for how well I was being Ben Franklin).

Mixed performance overall. But Franklin struggled too. As he wrote in his autobiography: “I was surprised to find myself so much fuller of faults than I imagined.”

Would I recommend Franklin’s wellness routine? Yes! Being mindful of what you eat , getting enough exercise and focusing on personal growth are as helpful today as they were 250 years ago.

But our understanding of health and the body has progressed significantly since then. Today, instead of wildly swinging around dumbbells, Franklin might be following a customized strength training plan. RIP, Ben Franklin – you would have made an amazing TikTok wellness influencer.

The autobiography is a pleasant read and funnier than I expected. There’s one scene where Franklin somehow acquires too many bread rolls from a baker and runs into his future father-in-law, one roll under each arm and one in his mouth. “I made a most awkward, ridiculous appearance,” he says. What a goof, haha.
In the interest of journalistic integrity, I decide to check whether Franklin was indeed the aspirational lifestyle model he presented himself to be.

“We forget how vital and healthy [Franklin] was into his 50s,” says Rae Katherine Eighmey, food historian and author of Stirring the Pot with Benjamin Franklin: A Founding Father’s Culinary Adventures.

Franklin emphasized the importance of regular physical activity, especially if one had a relatively sedentary job, as he did. Similarly, he was adamant about paying attention to what one ate and drank, and the effects of alcohol. The latter was particularly notable at a time when diets were rich in alcohol and it was considered healthy to take a shot of liquor first thing in the morning, says Sarah Lohman, food historian and author.

Over the years, Franklin suffered from gout, psoriasis , pleurisy and bladder stones . But according to Adelman, “he does seem to have been, all things told, for an 18th-century white man, relatively healthy.”

Franklin loved an early morning (as Poor Richard, he coined the phrase: Early to bed and early to rise makes a man healthy, wealthy and wise). According to the daily schedule he shared in his autobiography, Franklin awoke most days at 5am. His morning routine lasted about two hours, and consisted of the following:
“Rise, wash, and address Powerful Goodness ! [Ed note: his version of God/a higher power] Contrive day’s business, and take the resolution of the day; prosecute the present study, and breakfast.”

I was an early riser for many years. I would wake up before the sun and go to an exercise class, or start writing for work. But then I got pregnant, and a small alien in my uterus began gobbling up my life force. Then, my ideal amount of sleep changed to between 18 and 30 hours a day. It became all I could do to get out of bed and have my one weak cup of coffee.

Still, to honor my friend Ben, I set my alarm for my version of 5am, which is 7am. When it goes off, I roll out of bed with much moaning and groaning, and wash my face. I try to address my own Powerful Goodness, but I’m not great spiritual company because I’m so tired. I settle for saying, “Thanks for, you know, everything,” to the universe.

Franklin enjoyed “air baths”, Eighmey told me. These entailed “sitting naked shortly after arising in front of an open window”. This sounds kind of nice, actually, but unfortunately our windows all look into the apartment of our neighbor, a nice woman in her 60s whose cat was recently diagnosed with cancer. I decided she has enough on her plate without having to see me air bathing, so I skip it.

According to a quick Google search, “to prosecute the present study” means to spend time actively learning or working on a personal project, so I watch TikToks about the Love Is Blind reunion and text my thoughts to my husband – an honest-to-goodness early riser who is already at his office. (I detail why I’m rooting for Jax and Stew; he agrees climbing four volcanoes in a year is not enough to make Captain Blake interesting and that Erika deserves better.)

I have my usual wheat cereal with yogurt and berries, a low-effort meal that has nutrients the alien inside me needs. But I wish I were having Franklin’s favorite breakfast, which Eighemy tells me was fresh bread cubes tossed in melted butter, toasted, then dropped in a bowl of hot wheat cereal and topped with more butter. Yum! I might make this for myself sometime when I’m sad.

From 8am to 11am, Franklin worked. I do this too. Twins! I am mostly coherent on my calls, and make some good jokes in the work Slack (admittedly, one is just pointing out a picture of a guy in a funny hat), so I consider it a successful morning. Franklin once wrote a satirical essay all about farting , so he would have probably had some good Slack bits too.

Franklin took a two-hour lunch every day, which feels extremely luxurious. Lunch was the biggest meal of the day in Franklin’s time, said Lohman. It’s unclear what he ate most days, but according to his writings, his favorite foods included potatoes, parmesan and apples. I have some beef and potato stew I made over the weekend, which feels like the sort of heavy, solemn dish early American colonists would have eaten, and follow it up with an apple.

I need a nap after my heavy meal. But first, I must “overlook my accounts”, as Franklin said he did at midday. I open the banking app on my phone, feel slightly depressed at the small number I discover there, then sleep for 30 minutes. Franklin did not usually take naps, but he merely gestated a democracy, not a human child.

Physical activity was important to Franklin. I don’t have access to a pool or a stable to go riding – two of his favorite pastimes – but I do have dumbbells, which Franklin once wrote to his son , William, contain “a great quantity of exercise in a handful of minutes”. Franklin said he would do 40 swings with them, gripping one weight in each hand and swinging them back and forth by his sides.

I find a video of a man in a Franklin costume (no wig, sadly) demonstrating the exercise. After laughing for a while because it looks so silly, I try it myself. Although I fear it will cause a shoulder injury, the exercise is now known as “ skier swings ”, and various fitness blogs recommend it, as long as you keep the weight low.

When I do the exercise, I stop laughing. It’s harder than it looks and I tire out after 30 reps. I wonder whether Franklin had powerful shoulders, and I look up pictures of him, but the little jackets he wore didn’t really do his upper body justice. His calves looked rather shapely though.
Franklin and I both clock out at 6pm. From then until 10pm, Franklin went about his evening routine:
“Put things in their places, supper, music, or diversion, or conversation; examination of the day.”

As I empty the dishwasher, I imagine Franklin arranging all his little knick-knacks. But when I research what his homes were like, I find that a 1998 excavation of his terrace house in London uncovered not just knick-knacks, but a pit full of over 1200 human and animal bones. Apparently William Hewson, the son-in-law of Franklin’s landlady, ran an anatomy school from the house. Franklin seems to have been fine with this – he described the anatomist as an “excellent young man”.
After supping and conversing with my husband, I sit down to determine how my experiment has gone.

My strengths, I decided, were “order” (I basically stuck to Franklin’s schedule and accomplished my work tasks), “frugality” (I didn’t order an expensive sweater I wanted) and “cleanliness” (emptied dishwasher, wiped down kitchen counters). My weaknesses were “temperance” (a virtue Franklin describes as eating “not to dullness”, but I was decidedly dull after lunch), “silence” (I did not avoid “trifling conversation” – in fact, I actively sought it out) and “humility” (I praised myself throughout the day for how well I was being Ben Franklin).
Mixed performance overall. But Franklin struggled too. As he wrote in his autobiography: “I was surprised to find myself so much fuller of faults than I imagined.”
Would I recommend Franklin’s wellness routine? Yes! Being mindful of what you eat , getting enough exercise and focusing on personal growth are as helpful today as they were 250 years ago.

But our understanding of health and the body has progressed significantly since then. Today, instead of wildly swinging around dumbbells, Franklin might be following a customized strength training plan. RIP, Ben Franklin – you would have made an amazing TikTok wellness influencer.

articles.title: Senegal restored as Africa Cup of Nations champions after court ruling
articles.summary: Senegal won January’s final 1-0 after walking off Result was overturned in March as 3-0 win for Morocco Senegal have been restored as the Africa Cup of Nations champions after a ruling by the court of arbitration for sport (Cas). Senegal beat Morocco 1-0 in a chaotic Afcon final in January but the result was overturned two months later as a 3-0 default win for Morocco by an appeals panel appointed by the Confederation of African Football (Caf). Continue reading...
articles.content:
Senegal have been reinstated as the champions of Africa, and their controversial 1-0 victory over Morocco confirmed in the record books, after the scandal over January’s Africa Cup of Nations final was resolved in a Swiss courtroom.

The court of arbitration for sport (Cas) ruled that a decision to award the 2025 Afcon title to Morocco on appeal should be set aside. Senegal celebrated with a social media post proclaiming the team to have won the title twice: first on the field and then at Cas. Morocco, who are due to co-host the World Cup in 2030, declared their intention to “pursue all legal avenues” to challenge the ruling.

A Cas panel of three legal experts agreed unanimously that the original result should stand because of the primacy of decisions made on “the field of play”. The referee’s decision to complete the fixture was held to be a definitive act that could not be overturned by Senegal’s breach of Afcon’s rules when they walked off and caused a 15-minute delay in one of the most notorious encounters in the competition’s history.

In the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.

If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.

If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from the iOS App Store on iPhone or the Google Play store on Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.

The final was held in the Moroccan city of Rabat on 18 January. With the match goalless in second-half added time, the then Senegal coach, Pape Thiaw, withdrew his team from the field in protest at Morocco being awarded a penalty, shortly after Senegal had had a goal disallowed. After Senegal returned to the pitch, Brahim Díaz missed the spot kick with a Panenka. Senegal went on to win with a goal in extra time.

The result caused huge ructions in African football and became a media sensation. An initial appeal by the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) to the Confederation of African Football (Caf) argued that Senegal’s behaviour had contravened Afcon rules which prevent teams from leaving the field without the referee’s authorisation. The argument was accepted by Caf, which overturned the result in March, awarding Morocco the title in a 3-0 walkover.

Senegal responded with an appeal, and an in-person hearing took place behind closed doors at Cas on 8 October. Cas verdicts can be challenged at Switzerland’s supreme court only on limited procedural grounds.

The judging panel concluded that the “field of play doctrine” which prevents the court from reviewing decisions taken on the pitch by match officials must hold sway, and that because referee, Jean-Jacques Ndala, had not chosen to call the match off the result should stand.

“ By blowing his whistle to resume his match at the 109th minute the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met,” said Matthieu Reeb, the director general of CAS. “Both teams were on the pitch again and both expressed their willingness to resume. The Cas panel found that the referee’s decision fell solely within the scope of the rules of the game and was therefore within his sole authority. The Caf rules [Afcon regulations] would have been applicable if the referee had blown the final whistle which would have resulted in Senegal’s forfeit loss, but this was not the case.”

In a trenchant statement the FRMF announced its determination to continue fighting the result, saying it “reaffirms its determination to pursue all available legal avenues to challenge this Cas decision”.

The FRMF argued that the Cas decision “failed to take into account the stance recently adopted by both the International Football Association Board (Ifab) and the International Federation of Association Football (Fifa) regarding players leaving the field of play without the referee’s authorisation, as well as the associated responsibilities and disciplinary sanctions.”

It also expressed “astonishment” that Cas had not delayed its verdict after being presented with claims by the FRMF that one of the three panel members, professor Dr Ulrich Haas, had had a private telephone conversation with the president of the Senegalese Football Federation on Sunday.

Cas said: “The [international council of arbitration for sport] challenge commission found that there was not enough evidence at the time of the challenge to delay the issuing of the decision. Ulrich Haas strongly denies any direct contact at any moment with the parties involved in this procedure.”

Senegal’s Sadio Mané said on Instagram that the Cas decision “fills us with joy”. He spoke of the “efforts and sacrifices everyone has put into for this second star” and thanked fans for their support. He also expressed solidarity with Morocco, saying: “Senegal and Morocco are two brother peoples. May the passion of football continue to bring us closer.”

articles.title: Dynamic pricing to be used for games in US during 2031 Women’s World Cup
articles.summary: Ticketing model was in place for 2026 men’s World Cup Fans criticized system but Fifa saw record revenues A dynamic pricing model is set to be used in ticket sales for games held in the United States at the 2031 Women’s World Cup , which will be co-hosted with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica. Sources involved with the bid, which was formally ratified by Fifa on Monday, have told the Guardian it is inevitable that variable pricing will be used in the US after its successful application at last summer’s men’s World Cup, which generated about $5bn in ticket sales and hospitality, a significant increase on Fifa’s projection of $3.3bn. Continue reading...
articles.content:
A dynamic pricing model is set to be used in ticket sales for games held in the United States at the 2031 Women’s World Cup , which will be co-hosted with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica.

Sources involved with the bid, which was formally ratified by Fifa on Monday, have told the Guardian it is inevitable that variable pricing will be used in the US after its successful application at last summer’s men’s World Cup, which generated about $5bn in ticket sales and hospitality, a significant increase on Fifa’s projection of $3.3bn.

The sources add that the US market is a special case as dynamic pricing, which sees the price of tickets to events fluctuate based on demand, is widely accepted due to the ubiquity of secondary ticketing and resale platforms without any price cap.

The 2031 bid book does not mention dynamic pricing but is projecting revenues of $550m from ticket sales – more than 10 times the $43m grossed at the 2023 World Cup in Australia and New Zealand – plus $300m in hospitality income and a further $400m in other matchday revenue.

US Soccer president Cindy Parlow Cone said after the bid’s ratification that those projections were “extremely conservative”, while Fifa’s Evaluation Report states: “Based on the performance of other recent tournaments hosted in the region, most notably the Fifa World Cup 2026, gate revenues may far exceed initial projections.”

Fifa declined to comment, but sources insisted it is far too early for a decision on ticket pricing. Prices will not be set until 2030.

Other Fifa sources added that the governing body would comply with each host country’s government regulations and adapt to local customs, which in the US is likely to include dynamic pricing. Ticket resale laws are stricter in Mexico and there may not be sufficient demand for fluctuating sales markets in Costa Rica and Jamaica.

Fifa was widely criticized when it announced that it would be used at the men’s World Cup, triggering claims of “price gouging” and fears of empty seats at some matches, but the overall occupancy rate was above 99% and revenue soared.

In addition to maximizing revenues Fifa also pointed out that introducing an official ticket resale platform was an attempt to limit ticket touting, where official tickets are sold on for personal profit. While Fifa was criticized for taking 15% commission from both the seller and the buyer on its resale platform, the organization has argued that all those funds are reinvested into football unlike the proceeds of touting.

Dynamic pricing will not be used at next summer’s Women’s World Cup in Brazil and may not feature at the 2030 men’s tournament in Morocco, Spain and Portugal. Uefa has ruled it out for the 2028 men’s Euros, to be hosted by England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland.

There has not been a decision on the 2035 Women’s World Cup , which was awarded on Monday to England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

“At the moment, the model is absolutely that Fifa decides those things,” said Sue Day, the Football Association’s director of women’s football, on Monday. “We will hope to be able to have a really strong influence on some of that because we know our audiences best.”

Continue reading...
articles.content:
Midfielder is preparing to face Liverpool after leaving the club he loves and overcoming a tough start in Belgium

I n April Freddie Potts was absorbing the disappointment of being substituted at half-time during West Ham’s FA Cup quarter-final defeat by Leeds. The midfielder was out of favour under Nuno Espírito Santo and could not have imagined that he would be preparing to face Liverpool in the Champions League seven months later.

It is the 23-year-old’s reward for taking the difficult decision to leave his boyhood club last summer. Potts noticed his minutes were drying up in pre-season, even though West Ham were not exactly stocked with talent after relegation, and was ready for a new challenge when Club Brugge offered about £10m to sign him.

“I thought this was the perfect place for me to take the next step,” Potts says of his move to the Belgian champions. “I’m not going to shy away – it was very hard. West Ham have been my club for my whole life. I still have a lot of love for West Ham. But I had to take into account what was best for my career and I’m loving it at Brugge.

“Every player wants to be in the team expected to win every week, and seeing how Club Brugge have performed in the Champions League before shows the project and how they want to develop the team and players. It was a very exciting place for me to come. They look to develop young players.”

Potts was six when he joined West Ham. His father, Steve, made 506 appearances for the club and is part of Scott Parker’s backroom staff now. His brother, Dan, came through the academy before moving to Luton in 2015. This is a West Ham family; it is no surprise that moving to Belgium was emotional for Potts.

Yet it was the right move. Brugge are second in the Belgian Pro League, a point behind Union Saint‑Gilloise, and have impressed in the Champions League. They have nine points from four games in the league phase and caused a stir when they beat Inter 4-3 at San Siro last month.

Potts calls it “one of the best nights of my career”. It was quite the turnaround for a player who mostly watched from the bench as West Ham tried to save themselves during the second half of last season. It helps that Potts knows how to stay calm. He was talked up as a future West Ham captain when he made his full debut and impressed in a 3-1 win over Newcastle last year. He had a run in the team but lost his place when Nuno switched to a 4-4-2 in January and settled on Mateus Fernandes and Tomas Soucek as his preferred partnership in central midfield.

That was when Potts remembered how he grew during loan spells at Portsmouth and Wycombe. “I know that you can have games where you feel like you are on top of the world, and then you can come straight back down,” he says. “The loans helped me out massively with West Ham because I managed to cope with the highs. The Newcastle game was a real high, but there were some lows after that and I feel like I was coping with it.”

Potts saw the reaction on social media when he left. Some West Ham fans were not happy with the club for allowing a homegrown player to depart. This season has been tough for West Ham, who are ninth in the Championship after a disappointing run and replaced Nuno with Parker this month. One problem has been the lack of a No 6. Potts, who can snap into a tackle and link play from deep, has been watching from afar.

“I still think they’re playing well,” he says. “They’ve got a great team, great players. I think Scott Parker is a really good manager and he’s got three teams promoted from the Championship. I don’t think it will be a problem again. West Ham will get promoted in the end.”

Potts has glitzier assignments and is adjusting to his surroundings. He cannot speak much Flemish but he has sipped a couple of Belgian beers and is enjoying life in Bruges. “I’m not going to lie, when I first joined I found it difficult. It’s completely different when you move country. But I was open to the challenge. At the start it was a challenge but now it’s really smooth.”

One of the biggest challenges has been adapting to a new style. Given the intensity of the Premier League it is a surprise to hear Potts say Brugge, managed by the 48-year‑old Croat Ivan Leko, have helped him become more physical.

articles.content:
Festive drinks are all about capturing the warmth and theatre of the season, so lean into wintry flavours such as orange and cloves, and add a bit of drama by bringing out the blowtorch

What are the best cocktails to make for a Christmas party? Dan, by email We’re all in favour of getting the party season started early, Dan, so now is as good a time as any to get your drinks cupboard in order. “Ultimately, Christmas cocktails are all about bringing a little warmth, nostalgia and theatre, so don’t be afraid to have fun with seasonal flavours,” says Josie Pink, author of River Cottage: Cocktails and Botanicals . The smell of orange, be it fresh or dried, is never too far away at this time of year, and one reason Pink suggests having a batch of orange liquor on hand, not least “to rustle up a margarita or two”. Ditto dried citrus wheels: “They’re a must,” she says. “Not only are they gorgeous for adorning cocktails, but any misshapes can be turned into marmalade dust, and any spares into home decorations.” Pink also advises getting some syrups in your arsenal – “I’d opt for a batch of trusty vanilla syrup” – plus a chai number “for those fragrant, warming spice flavours that we all associate with the festive season”.

If there’s a gang coming over, you’ll likely find Pink ladling hot mulled apple juice laced with citrussy gin into mugs, or making pitchers of rum punch: “Either would warm the cockles.” Alternatively, consider a “slightly lighter” mulled white wine: “Gently warm your favourite white wine with spices such as star anise, cinnamon, ginger and cloves, sweeten with syrup and citrus, then spike with apple cider brandy.”

At the other end of the temperature scale, make like Fabio Iacovino, bar manager at Celeste in west London, with a frosted monkey punch. To serve about 20, he combines 600ml gin ( Monkey 47 for preference), 500ml fresh lemon juice, 300ml gingerbread syrup ( Monin ), 200ml almond grappa ( Nardini ) and 500ml chilled filtered water in a jug, then chills in the fridge. “Make it on the day, though,” he warns, because “anything with fresh lemon juice is always best drunk within about six hours”. Pour the lot into a punch bowl over a large block of ice – “it melts slowly and keeps dilution under control” – and garnish with orange wheels and a few cinnamon sticks. To serve, ladle 100ml punch over ice (in punch cups or rocks glasses, for preference) and grate fresh nutmeg on top.

Smaller gatherings, meanwhile, might call for espresso martinis. “I’d use a chai syrup to give this classic crowd-pleaser the festive twist it deserves,” Pink says. “But a bit of flair never goes amiss, so I might go for something that calls for a blowtorch.” A spiced bourbon creme brulee would tick that box nicely: put cream liqueur and chai syrup in a shaker, fill it three-quarters of the way with ice, then add bourbon and lemon juice. “Once shaken and strained, dust with icing sugar and wave a blowtorch over the top to caramelise.” Carefully, mind.

That said, we all know nothing hugs and cossets in winter quite like an apple crumble, so why not capture that vibe in drinks form? “With cloudy apple juice, amaretto and spiced rum, it’s full of nostalgic flavours and always goes down a treat,” Pink says. You could even get all fancy by decorating the glass with a digestive biscuit rim and an apple slice dusted with sugar, “torched to order”. Well, it is Christmas, after all.

articles.title: GTA VI’s jaw-dropping success: in figures
articles.summary: Content creators have produced hundreds of millions of hours of video game since its launch Grand Theft Auto ( GTA) VI became the largest video game release of all time last week and while it is hard to say exactly how many people are playing the game (current estimates say at least 30 million), there are plenty of other jaw-dropping data points we do know. Data on streaming the game suggests that only two days into its release a cumulative 364.5m hours have been watched – roughly 41,000 years of content. Put another way, that translates to more than 41,000 years worth of people riffling through cash registers, hanging drywall, birding, diving or hijacking jets. That’s according to streaming data from Streams Charts, a data and analytics company that has been tracking Rockstar Game’s long-awaited title. Continue reading...
articles.content:
Content creators have produced hundreds of millions of hours of video game since its launch

G rand Theft Auto ( GTA) VI became the largest video game release of all time last week and while it is hard to say exactly how many people are playing the game (current estimates say at least 30 million), there are plenty of other jaw-dropping data points we do know.

Since releasing last Thursday on PS5 and Xbox game consoles, Sony’s reported pre-sales of 32.5m units amounts to the biggest entertainment release across all mediums. It made $3.8bn in its first day alone.

Online streaming platforms like Twitch, YouTube and Kick make up a major share of how people are tuning into the franchise.

Those who grew up playing video games know that watching people play goes hand in hand with the activity. For this writer, that’s a memory of me and my three brothers struggling for the best viewing angle as we took turns huddled around the original Game Boy.

For Gen Z and Alpha, who grew up in the era of social media, it has been watching folks muck about on popular titles like Minecraft, Fortnite or GTA’s previous iterations.

Notably, there are many platforms to watch gameplay in realtime – including Twitch, YouTube or Kick – and for some, there is real money to be made. Since streaming platforms have monetized, the global market size is projected to be $13.3bn in 2026, according to Grand View Research , a business consulting firm.

The exclusivity of the game, which isn’t available on PC or Nintendo Switch at this point, has also fueled some of the novelty. Looking at average viewership since its launch, it’s possible many of the early backseat gamers might have only wanted to see the game that has been in development for 13 years . Some viewers have also likely moved on to becoming players.

When compared against the next top 10 game releases by their viewership, GTA VI stands apart as a cultural phenomenon. It has more viewership than the next top three titles combined. And we aren’t at a full week of data yet.

GTA VI’s launch viewership is more than twice that of Valorant, a team-based and free-to-play shooting game. Or, put another way, more viewers than the next three combined.

When we think of gaming, we think of the immersive experience itself: Donning a new persona and living out an alternate reality. It turns out that in addition to being the best selling video game of all time, it’s also the most watched release.
